Open items

For Amelia to decide. The 57 findings behind most of these are in _scratch/combo-review.md (gitignored, 2026-10-31), with real generated sentences and per-1,000 rates. Its replacement words are suggestions, not checked against the banks.

  • Replace “barely legal” in the modern bizarre adjectives? It carries a sexual connotation at the clean default and also gives “barely legal and illegal in three states”. Suggestions: “legally distinct”, “legally ambiguous”, “technically permitted”.
  • Mass nouns after “a”: replace the words, or stop those templates putting “a” before a subject? Sincere: kindness, creativity, curiosity, judgment, energy (together about 130 of every 1,000 plain compliment() calls). Grumpy: attendance, small talk, work, meeting behavior. Quirky, by blending: playlist curation, group chat etiquette. Shakespearean cheerful: merriment, laughter, revelry. Shakespearean sincere: constancy.
  • “remarkably” with adjectives that already carry an adverb (“a remarkably not entirely terrible attendance”): drop “remarkably” from the sincere and grumpy templates and use {a}, or keep it for one-word adjectives only?
  • Blunt grumpy group: 2 of the 7 grumpy templates, so about 287 of every 1,000 grumpy calls (measured with _scratch/build_check.R), up from about 164 for onerous and uninspired alone. Add more templates, or give the group a lower share?
  • Suffixes after “and yet” read badly: “Nobody asked for your joyless attendance, and yet, and I mean it, darn it.” Reword the template, or keep the trailing clause off it?
  • dance move reads oddly in the singular (about 85 of every 1,000 cheerful calls). Replace it?
  • Shakespearean vocabulary: change labor to labour, and cosmicall and shadowe to real words (“celestial”, “shade”)?
  • Profanity: “, as heck” usually lands after a noun (about 1 in 6 mild outputs); move it to the intensifier path or drop it? Should an intensifier go before the last word of a multi-word adjective rather than the first (“your damn borderline impressive excuse”)? Give Shakespearean its own intensifiers and suffixes, so “thy” and “you” stop colliding?
  • Combo review findings marked keep or low priority still need your yes: glory, energy, raccoons in Shakespearean, ether-signal, thunderous, sunny + “ray of sunshine”, unconquerable, radiant, -ly adjectives after “officially”.
  • Templates use a double hyphen (--) in places. Noticed, not reviewed. Keep it?
  • The expanded word lists were chosen by an agent and no person has read them. Do you want to review them before they ship?
  • dev-history.md has em dashes, kept because it records history. Replace them too?
  • apply_profanity() puts the intensifier before the first plain-text match of the adjective in the finished sentence. No current adjective appears inside a template or subject it can pair with (checked by the 2026-11-03 branch review), but a new word could, and the stem check does not catch it for adjectives under four letters (fey). Insert the intensifier at the {adjective} placeholder instead, before the adjective is substituted?
  • compliment() treats a template as a group’s when its group has no subjects (is.null(group$subjects)). If a group is ever given subjects, its templates would quietly draw the bank’s adjectives instead of the group’s. Have pick_group() say directly that it picked a group? (/code-review, 2026-11-03)
  • The repeated-word check skips words under four letters, so fey, jig, hat or wit could repeat elsewhere in a sentence. Compare short words whole? (/code-review, 2026-11-03)
  • farewell() and farewell_of_the_day() have no weirdness argument: farewells are whole fixed sentences (four or five per mood), not templates filled from word lists, so there is nothing to blend. Add one? It would need quirky and bizarre farewell lines and the same tier weighting compliment() uses.
  • compliment(weirdness = NA) fails with R’s own “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” instead of the package’s message, and compliment(n = Inf) warns “NAs introduced by coercion” before failing. Check is.na() and is.finite() in the argument checks? (Predates this branch; third review, 2026-11-04.)
  • The four-letter check blocks some words that are not repeats: “doorknob charisma” can never fill “…has strong main-character energy.” because “char” matches “character”. Accept it, or compare longer stems for some words? (Third review, 2026-11-04.)
  • aura's aura repeats a word within one entry, which the check never compares with itself. Keep it as a deliberate joke? (Third review, 2026-11-04.)
  • The profanity docs say profanity is added as an intensifier or a trailing clause, but apply_profanity() now returns the sentence unchanged when every candidate repeats a word. Not shown to happen with a real bank sentence. Mention it in the docs? (Third review, 2026-11-04.)
  • indefinite_article() gives “an” for “oneself” and “ewe”, both wrong; neither is in the banks. Extend the y/w list if such words are added? (Third review, 2026-11-04.)
  • The pkgdown deploy now uses clean: true, which deletes any file on gh-pages that docs/ does not contain. Judged safe from a local origin/gh-pages ref that may be stale; check the live gh-pages branch for anything not from pkgdown (a CNAME, for one) before the next deploy to main? (Third review, 2026-11-04.)
  • Speed: stems_clash() recomputes the template’s word stems on every redraw, and 20,000 grumpy calls at weirdness 0.25 take about 9 seconds (branch review, 2026-11-03). Compute the template’s stems once before the redraw loop?
